description: Audits one Google Business Profile against every Local SEO check: profile basics, categories, description, services and attributes, photos, reviews, posts, the linked website and trust signals, with a 0-100 score. Use it for a profile audit or to confirm a fix. include picks what is read beyond the profile; keyword adds the relevance checks and is the competitor search. It works in the user's own Chrome through the Local SEO extension, opening Google Maps in a background tab, and fails with a message saying how to connect when the extension is not connected. Nothing is written to Google. It can take a few minutes. Returns business (the full profile record), findings, score (an object: score, 0-100, or null when no check could be judged; judged, the number of checks judged; untested, the number not_applicable), fixes (checkId, title, severity, fix; most important first), reportMarkdown (the whole audit as a readable report) and notes on what was not read, including when Maps showed the page in a language other than English, which leaves some fields missing. The audit reads posts in the browser, which sees only the newest one, so the posting checks (L26 to L29) are not_applicable with the reason; read_posts with source dataforseo reads them all. When Maps keeps its own "Most relevant" review order, a note says so and the recency checks (L22 recent reviews, L24 reply speed, L25 recent unanswered negatives unless one was found) are not_applicable. Each finding has checkId (a Local SEO check id such as L7), group, status (pass, partial, fail or not_applicable), severity (high, medium or low on a fail or partial, null otherwise), a one-sentence summary and evidence (url, value, note). not_applicable means the check could not be judged, never that it passed or failed. A profile field the page or provider did not give is {missing: true, reason}; with absent: true it means Google was read and lists nothing there (no phone on the profile), which is a real gap, while without it the value is simply unknown. Never treat either as 0.

mapsUrl.description: A Google Maps link to the place, such as https://maps.app.goo.gl/... .

placeId.description: A Google place id, such as "ChIJ...".

cid.description: A Google customer id (CID), decimal digits, as in maps.google.com/?cid=.

city.description: The town or city it is in, such as "Leeds, UK".

name.description: The business name as Google shows it.

business.description: Which business: exactly one of {mapsUrl}, {placeId}, {cid} or {name, city}. Ids from find_business or local_scan are exact; a name and city is searched in Maps and can match a different place with the same name.

include.description: What to read beyond the profile: reviews, posts, website (the linked page, for the NAP and schema checks) and competitors (the Maps results for keyword, or for the primary category without one). Defaults to ["reviews", "posts", "website"]. A part left out makes its checks not_applicable.

keyword.description: The search the business wants to rank for, such as "emergency plumber". Used by the relevance checks and, with include competitors, as the competitor search. Defaults to none, which leaves the keyword checks not_applicable.

name: audit_profile
title: Audit a Business Profile
